In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have presented necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of distributed containment control algorithms without the velocity measurements of followers for the case when the leaders are static or dynamic under both fixed and time-varying directed network topologies in a space of an arbitrary finite dimension.

, for the distributed containment control of multiple mobile agents in high dimensional space under fixed or switching network topology, if the agents have velocity measurements, then the agents can be designed to converge to the convex or hyperrectangle that contains all the agents, but if the agents do not have velocity measurements, they can only be designed to converge in the best case scenario to the hyperrectangle that contains only the agents.

, for any high dimensional space, we have provided distributed containment control algorithms for both stationary and dynamic leaders without velocity measurements under both fixed and switchings directed network topologies and we have provided necessary and sufficient conditions for convergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a unified framework to study the distributed containment control of multiple agents with multiple stationary and dynamic leaders under both switching and fixed directed networks in any high dimensional Euclidean space.

the proposed distributed control algorithms are able to achieve the distributed containment control of multiple agents with multiple leaders in a space of finite dimension under both fixed and time varying network topologies.

we have developed a new coordinate transformation technique to facilitate the analysis of a class of high dimensional distributed control algorithms, and we have also proposed a distributed tracking control strategy without velocity measurements for multiple mobile agents under a switching network in a high dimensional Euclidean space.

the proposed distributed tracking control algorithm can guarantee convergence to the dynamic convex set formed by the leaders without velocity measurements, which has important implications on the practical implementation of the algorithm.
